items.title: Chazz Frichtel interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, June 13, 2016
items.q: She tried to get me to play with a pick, which I never — she really loved playing with a pick.

ctx.x: Did you meet those kind of studio guys who, they’d have a date from 10 to 2 and then they’d have a date from 2 to 5 somewhere else and they’re just trying to get from one place to the other.

Yeah absolutely. When I first got there, one of the first people I called, because I admired her so much, was Carol Kaye. And she was mostly teaching then, because the days of The Wrecking Crew had kind of given way to bands as opposed to hiring this incredible section of musicians that played on everything. But she was doing a lot of teaching. And she used to tell me about what her schedule was like in the day, and she’d have a ten o’clock call at Capitol and then she’d have a one o’clock call over at Emerald or…

I’m going to move your mic up a little bit and we’ll just edit this out. These things are so sensitive that they — see if that’s better. So you say, “Hey Carol, if you can’t make a date here I am, right?”
